rules.note: Scenes you come upon in the open, between one place and the next. See src/chronicle/roadside.gd. An event's `stage` is what stands a few cells ahead on the ground when it is come upon (D131): its props (art, offset from the scene's middle), and who is being set on (`victim`, a unit); its `pack` stand round them. A scene with `near_town` (D215) is the town's Watch beset: offered only within `town_reach` tiles of a standing town but, like every scene, never within `clear_of_sites` of a place (a ring of road out past its gate), at `near_town_chance` a step, the others only in open country at `chance`. Its stage's `allies` stand with it and fight beside the party; `purse_line` is how its purse is said. Since D216 a scene is stood `stage_cells` ahead, seen coming: its title goes in the log, what is going on there (`seen`) as the party comes within `tell_cells`, with no box, and a party walking itself is not stopped (walking aggressively it goes and steps in).

trader_ambush.title: A cart has been stopped on the road ahead.
seen: The horse is screaming before you see why.
A cart sits crossways in the ruts with its wheel off, and four of them are working the driver over with the butts of their spears.
Nobody down there has noticed you yet.
walked_by: You take the long way round the hill.
The noise stops before you are clear of it.
saved: They break before you have finished with them, which tells you what they were.
The driver comes out from under his cart with a split lip and both hands up.
asks: "You'll want paying," he says, counting it out on the boards. "Everyone does."
"But there's better than coin, if you've the patience. Get me and this cart as far as %s and I'll see you right, and keep seeing you right after."

burnt_wagon.title: Something is burning off the road.
seen: A wagon, still going up, and the ones who set it are stood watching it burn.
They have not bothered to move the driver out of the way of it.
walked_by: You keep the smoke on your left and say nothing about it at the next hearth.
saved: A woman crawls out of the ditch where she had the sense to go, and looks at the wagon, and then at you.
asks: "That was everything," she says. "All of it. Every bolt of it."
"There's a cousin in %s who owes me a start. Walk me there and you'll have a share of whatever I make after."

toll_post.title: Somebody has put a rope across the road.
seen: A rope, a fire, and three men who have decided this stretch is theirs.
They want a toll. They are not the sort who stop at a toll.
walked_by: You pay, because it is cheaper than the alternative, and it costs you the taste of it all afternoon.
saved: The rope comes down. The road is a road again.
Whatever they had taken off the last few through here is still in the sack by the fire.

watch_beset.title: The Watch is fighting on the road ahead.
seen: Steel on steel, and somebody shouting for help that is not coming.
Two of the Watch stand back to back in the road, and brigands are working round them on both sides.
They have not seen you yet. Neither have the Watch.
walked_by: You leave the road and keep low.
Somebody will ask the Watch, later, who walked past.
saved: The last of them runs for the grass.
The older of the two lowers his spear and looks you over. "We'll remember that," he says. "The Watch remembers."
watch_beset.purse_line: He presses %s on you: the Watch's bounty on their heads.

watch_wolves.title: The Watch has wolves on it, off the road.
seen: A horn, blown short and badly.
Two of the Watch have their backs to a wall by the road, and the wolves have learned to wait.
The wolves have not looked round yet.
walked_by: You go the long way round, upwind.
The horn sounds once more, then not again.
saved: The wolves break and go back to the open country.
"Thought that was us," says one of them, and laughs too long. "Thank you. Truly."
watch_wolves.purse_line: They empty a pouch into your hand: %s, all they have on them.
